title: Laughterton (1) Stirling Memorial
crew_summary: 7 crew — 7 killed including pilot Flg Off. Frederick Shaw Bradbury

external_narratives.summary: War Memorials Online registers the Laughterton Trentside Memorial, a stone cairn surmounted by a propeller blade and reduction gear with plaques on opposing sides. One side commemorates Stirling EH940 from 1661 HCU (pilot's first solo flight) which suffered an in-flight engine fire at 1,800 feet and crashed at Park Farm, Kettlethorpe on 21 June 1944. Five crew were killed and three injured.

external_narratives.summary: IWM registers the memorial as commemorating both Shorts Stirling EH940 and Avro Lancaster LM292. The memorial plaques on opposing sides were unveiled on 16 July 1994, erected on the village green beside the A1133.

memorial_details:
Flat-topped pyramid base of rough hewn stone, mounted in a grassed area, surmounted by single propeller blade and reduction gear. A dedicatory plaque is placed on face 1 in relation to EH940 and on face 3 for LM292.

The memorial was unveiled on the 16th July 1994 by the side of the A1133 and a unclassified road, erected by the local community.

Unveiling Ceremony (16th July 1994): The monument and plaques were unveiled to remember those lost in two local aircraft crashes during WWII.

Memorial Display: A display featuring Short Stirling EH940 and Avro Lancaster LM292 aircraft from World War II.
narrative: On 21 June 1944, Short Stirling EH940 from 1661 HCU, based at RAF Winthorpe, suffered an in-flight engine fire at 1,800 feet and crashed at Park Farm, Kettlethorpe. It was the pilot's first solo flight. Five crew were killed. In a separate incident on 8 August 1944, Lancaster LM292 from 103 Squadron, based at RAF Elsham Wold, was brought down near Fenton, claiming the lives of two crew members. The memorial, a stone cairn surmounted by a propeller blade and reduction gear, was unveiled on 16 July 1994.

Face 1 plaque: IN MEMORY OF
(5 names)
CREW OF SHORT STIRLING EH940 BASED AT RAF WINTHORPE
KILLED IN ACTION AT KETTLETHORPE
21st JUNE 1944
Face 2 tablet: IN MEMORY OF
(2 names)
CREW OF LANCASTER LM 292 FROM 103 SQUADRON
RAF ELSHAM WOLD
KILLED IN ACTION NEAR FENTON
8th AUGUST 1944
ON SUN TIPPED WINGS THEY LOVED TO FLY,
INTO THE WIDE UNMEASURED SKY
